answer.text:
At the solution demo and value workshop on 20 March 2024, Sofia Almeida said the shelf life field in the product master was "populated for maybe half the range" — an informal estimate, not a measurement. [1] [2]

At the technical due diligence on 18 April 2024, Priya Nair gave the same rough estimate — populated for maybe half — and added that some of the populated values were wrong, because nobody had owned the field since it was created. [3] [4] [5]

At the master data workshop on 24 September 2024, Kwame Boateng stated that shelf life is populated on 48% (T06U0025). He repeated the 48% figure in the remediation scope email of 30 September 2024, which listed "Shelf life populated 48%" for the pilot cohort of 4,214 articles and noted shelf life was out of scope for that phase (E13M006). Ana Duarte's steering note of 20 December 2024 recorded that shelf life remained at 48% and untouched for that phase (E13M002). [6] [7] [8]

At the fresh cutover call on 11 December 2025, Kwame Boateng stated the shelf life field is populated on 61% for the three categories in scope, up from 48%, because Priya's team did a pass in October (T18U0050, T18U0052). This is the latest population figure in the archive. [9] [10]

The 61% figure is scoped to the three in-scope fresh categories, so it is not directly comparable to the cohort-wide 48% figure. No later population figure appears in the archive through July 2026; the June 2026 reconciliation issue Nadia Haddad raised concerns extract totals versus till data for January to March, not the population rate (T22U0130, T22U0132). [10] [11] [12]

Recommendation: when quoting a figure, state its scope — 48% was cohort-wide (E13M006), 61% covers the three live fresh categories only (T18U0052) — and cite the 11 December 2025 cutover call as the current number, noting it is the latest recorded figure rather than one verified after that date. [7] [9] [10]

answer.question: What proportion of articles had shelf-life data populated? Give every figure in the archive with its date and source, and say which one is current.
trace: Read 2974 permitted source records at L3.

Verified all four figures against cited turns: 'maybe half' (T01U0049-T01U0050, Sofia Almeida), 'maybe half, and wrong for some' (T02U0105-T02U0107, Priya Nair), 48% (T06U0025 Kwame Boateng; E13M006; E13M002), 61% (T18U0050+T18U0052, Kwame Boateng).
Confirmed the interrupted sentence at T18U0050/T18U0052 is completed by the same speaker (Kwame Boateng), so 61% is attributed to him.
Confirmed the 48% figure appears in three records (2024-09-24 workshop, 2024-09-30 remediation scope email, 2024-12-20 steering note) and is consistent.
Checked for later population figures through July 2026; the June 2026 reconciliation issue (T22U0130, T22U0132) concerns extract totals vs till data, not population rate, so nothing supersedes 61%.
Distinguished informal estimates ('maybe half') from measured figures (48%, 61%) and preserved scope differences (cohort-wide vs three in-scope fresh categories).
Verified 12 quoted passages against runtime sources.
